Five myths about drought I keep hearing

February 3, 2025 · 4 min read

Every summer the same claims about drought come back around my town, usually repeated with total confidence. I spent a few weekends reading the actual reports, including the World Health Organization's material on water scarcity, and here is what I found.

Myth 1: drought only matters for farmers

Farmers feel it first, but reservoirs that supply cities drop too, and water rationing reached several large cities in southern Europe in 2023 and 2024. Hospitals and schools depend on the same municipal supply.

Myth 2: one wet winter ends a drought

Groundwater recovers far more slowly than surface water. A single rainy season can refill a reservoir while aquifers stay depleted for years, which is why hydrologists talk about multi-year recovery.
